prerequisites: Geometry of the real n-dimensional space

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the classification of different optimization problems.
Knowledge and understanding of the most important mathematical characterizations solutions to optimization problems.
Ability to formulate some classes of real problems in mathematical terms.
Ability to solve simple linear programming problems.
Ability to make autonomous choices in defining a mathematical programming model starting from a real decision problem.
Ability to describe the mathematical programming problems introduced in the course.
Ability to logically exhibit demonstrations of the theoretical properties studied.
Mastery of basic notions and methodologies, which allows for any further in-depth study of topics related to optimization.
Knowledge of data analysis tools and optimization techniques, including those based on artificial intelligence methods.
Aptitude for problem-solving and ability to work independently.
Ability to communicate, work in teams, and make decisions independently.
Ability to handle complex information and data obtained from multiple sources, and to analyze and manage multidisciplinary topics.
Ability to develop logical reasoning that, based on precise assumptions, leads to the demonstration of a thesis.

syllabus_topics: Linear programming models: allocation models and blending models
The minimum cost flow and the network simplex method
Use of binary variables to model logical constraints
Introduction to the Support Vector Machines

assessment_methods.method: Written test (multiple choice quizzes and pen and paper exercises)

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on the evaluation of either a written test (quizzes and exercises) or an oral test. A minimum passing grade is 18 out of 30. Honors (Laude) are awarded for outstanding work exceeding standard expectations.
